title: BreezeOn Application Definition
description: Authoritative machine contract for Step 1 application-definition inputs, defaults, and omission behavior. Human-readable explanation: application-development-process.md. Agents must consume this schema first; markdown is supporting documentation only.

repositoryName.description: GitHub repository name — lowercase kebab-case only (naming.md § Repositories). Examples: breezeon-corp-fin-inv, breezeon-system-admin-eac, standards. Do not use SCREAMING_CASE or PascalCase.

uniqueCode.description: EAC registry UniqueCode. Must equal repositoryName uppercased (ToUpperInvariant), e.g. breezeon-system-admin-eac → BREEZEON-SYSTEM-ADMIN-EAC. Do not invent a divergent id. Legacy UniqueCodes such as SYSTEM-ADMIN-EAC remain current registry reality until migration.

hostedAppRegistrationName.description: Shared customer-environment / BreezeOn-operated App Registration name for hosted hosts. No platform default — must be supplied.

localAppRegistrationName.description: Always BreezeOn-LOCAL for local development. Fixed platform value; not a free-form ask.

pages.description: Initial information architecture. Default when omitted: Home + New Request + Status Report + My Tasks.

applicationDisplayName.description: Human-readable product name (application-definition field; not part of Customer Branding or Application Branding packages). See docs/ui/shell/application-branding.md.

applicationLogo.description: Application Branding package — sole member. Locked filename app-logo.svg when omitted. Independent of Customer Branding.

customerName.description: Customer Branding — human-readable customer/tenant name. Displayed in expanded navigation to the right of the customer logo; hidden when navigation is minimized. Distinct from applicationDisplayName.

customerLogo.description: Customer Branding — authoritative source SVG filename. Locked name customer-logo.svg when omitted. Generates nav-logo.svg and favicon.svg; not independently user-configured placement assets.

primaryColor.description: Customer Branding theme input — six-digit #RRGGBB. Must be supplied together with secondaryColor and tertiaryColor, or all three omitted. Derived palette roles are never application-definition fields.

secondaryColor.description: Customer Branding theme input — six-digit #RRGGBB. Must be supplied together with primaryColor and tertiaryColor, or all three omitted.

tertiaryColor.description: Customer Branding theme input — six-digit #RRGGBB. Must be supplied together with primaryColor and secondaryColor, or all three omitted.

authority.conflictRule: If schema and markdown disagree, the schema is authoritative. Markdown must never introduce inputs, defaults, or behaviors absent from this schema.

themePersistence.rule: Only primaryColor, secondaryColor, and tertiaryColor may ever be persisted as user-configurable theme inputs in application-definition. Hover, pressed, selected, borders, foregrounds, dark variants, accessibility variants, and other generated colors are implementation outputs only and must never become application-definition fields. Future customization requests change palette-generation logic, not this schema.

modes.rule: Every application supports Light and Dark. Applications cannot add or remove theme modes through Step 1 configuration.

generatedCustomerAssets.rule: Placement-specific runtime bindings may differ but must derive from customer-logo.svg. nav-logo.svg and favicon.svg are never separate Step 1 user inputs.

omissionBehavior.pages: Use defaults.pages (Home + New Request + Status Report + My Tasks).
omissionBehavior.applicationLogo: Use locked filename app-logo.svg (platform/default or product asset).
omissionBehavior.customerName: Use defaults.customerName (BreezeOn). Expanded nav shows Customer Logo + Customer Name; minimized nav shows Customer Logo only.
omissionBehavior.customerLogo: Use locked filename customer-logo.svg; generate nav-logo.svg and favicon.svg from that source.
omissionBehavior.primaryColor_secondaryColor_tertiaryColo: If all three omitted, use complete platform-default Light and Dark palettes (application-theme-palette.md). If any one is supplied, all three are required (no partial palette).
omissionBehavior.pageSubtitles: Use standard reusable subtitles from application-branding.md.
omissionBehavior.brandingAssetFilenames: Rename customer uploads to customer-logo.svg; rename application uploads to app-logo.svg; never retain designer filenames. Generated placement files are always nav-logo.svg and favicon.svg.
omissionBehavior.generatedCustomerAssets: Derive nav-logo.svg and favicon.svg from customer-logo.svg; never collect them as separate Step 1 inputs.
omissionBehavior.browserTitle: Use <Page Title> - <Application Display Name> via BoDocumentTitle.
omissionBehavior.homeCardDescription: Equals the destination page subtitle (same string / resource key).
omissionBehavior.brandingPackages: Customer Branding = customerName + customerLogo + primaryColor + secondaryColor + tertiaryColor. Application Branding = applicationLogo only. applicationDisplayName is outside both packages.

agentConsumption: Consume this schema first for required / optional / defaults / omission behavior.
Use application-development-process.md as supporting documentation only (explanation, Steps 1–6, Distinctions).
Fill an instance from the user prompt; apply schema defaults for omitted optionals.

Ask only for missing non-defaulted required fields (repositoryName, uniqueCode, code, hostedAppRegistrationName, applicationDisplayName). Derive uniqueCode from repositoryName via ToUpperInvariant when not supplied.
Do not require customerName (default BreezeOn), customerLogo, or brand colors unless the user wants to customize Customer Branding.
Do not ask for navigationLogo, browserFavicon, themePalette, primaryHover, or any derived theme colors as Step 1 inputs.
If any of primaryColor / secondaryColor / tertiaryColor is supplied, require all three; otherwise omit all three and use platform default palettes.
Derive complete Light and Dark Theme Palettes from the three brand colors; never persist derived colors into the application-definition instance.
Do not require the user to read the markdown process doc to discover inputs.
Do not copy illustrative example instances (e.g. INV) as platform defaults.
